section: Viewing pipeline logs by using the OpenShift Logging Operator
job_statement: When I need to troubleshoot and audit pipeline executions, I want to access pipeline logs independently of pod lifecycle, so I can review logs even after pods are deleted
desired_outcomes: Minimize time required to locate relevant pipeline logs
Reduce resource consumption from retaining unnecessary pods
Ensure logs remain accessible for audit requirements
Eliminate dependency on pod availability for log access
evidence: viewing-pipeline-logs-using-the-openshift-logging-operator-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Lines 59-69: Assembly abstract explains the core problem (pods are deleted, logs needed) and solution (Elasticsearch Kibana stack)
notes: Main job covers the overall goal of accessing pipeline logs via Kibana instead of relying on pods

job_statement: As a cluster administrator, when I need to access pipeline logs through Kibana, I want to configure index patterns and filters, so I can efficiently query and view pipeline execution logs
parent_job: Access pipeline logs independently of pod lifecycle
prerequisites: Logs for pipeline runs and task runs are available
desired_outcomes: Minimize time to set up Kibana for pipeline log viewing
Ensure only relevant pipeline logs are displayed
Maximize visibility of pipeline run context in log messages
evidence: viewing-pipeline-logs-using-the-openshift-logging-operator-self-managed-reduced.adoc -> Lines 78-183: Complete procedure for viewing pipeline logs in Kibana, including prerequisites (lines 85-94), creating index patterns (lines 101-106), and adding filters (lines 107-182)
notes: User story provides the specific CLI and UI approach for the main job. Includes detailed filter examples for Tekton pipelines.
